title: Kernel Sampling Sculptor: arch-and-length-aware microkernel selection with staged warmstarts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We observe tail-latency variance across heterogeneous GPU instance types and mixed sequence-length workloads. Existing heuristics either pick conservative kernels (wasting cost) or overfit to average latency (causing tail SLA misses).

Goal: Build a lightweight online mechanism — the Kernel Sampling Sculptor — that sculpts a small candidate set of microkernels per model + shard using architecture fingerprint and sequence-length histogram, uses staged warmstart probes to gather microbenchmarks, and dynamically weights kernels during live routing to reduce 95th percentile latency while preserving cost efficiency.

This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout experiments for the Sculptor: integration into runtime decision path, telemetry hooks, and safe fallback rules.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Sculptor can generate per-model kernel candidate lists within 100ms of initial load.
2) Online probes (staged warmstarts) complete without increasing cold-start tail by >5%.
3) Deployed canary shows >=10% improvement in p95 latency on mixed-length synthetic traces vs current baseline, with <=2% increase in avg GPU utilization.
4) Integration exposes kernel choice rationale in console (per-request tag) for at least 7 days of history.
technical_notes:
High-level approach: 1) Fingerprint: capture small static features (arch, SM count, memory bandwidth proxy) + dynamic features (recent seq-len histogram, kv-cache hit ratios). 2) Candidate generation: query a compact catalog of microkernel descriptors and prune via cheap cost-estimator. 3) Staged warmstart probing: run 3 microbench probes per candidate using low-priority background slots or short-lived warmstart batches to collect latency/occupancy metrics. 4) Sculpted weights: compute softmax over negative latency+cost score to pick hedged routing distribution; include an exploration factor for long-tail drift. 5) Safety: maintain fallback to stable kernel and circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid cascading regressions.

Implementation notes: keep probes bounded (time and GPU ops), persist lightweight stats (ring buffer) for each model-shard combination, expose feature vector in trace spans. Avoid heavy state in control plane — prefer per-node local caches with TTL and reconcile on model load.
experiments:
- Phase A (local perf lab): run sculptor prototype against archived synthetic traces (short/long sequences, conversational bursts) to validate ranking correlates with microbench.
- Phase B (canary on small host pool): enable staged warmstarts on 5% of requests for 48h, collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.
- Phase C (gradual ramp): expand to 20% with rollback triggers on >10% p95 regression.

Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, probe overhead (ops/sec), decision-time per request, route stability (% of requests switching kernel in-flight), and operator-visible reason tags.
rollout_plan:
1) Prototype merged to experimental branch with feature flag.
2) Internal perf lab runs and review (2 sprints).
3) Canary on non-critical region (1 week) with automated rollback.
4) Metrics review with SRE and PM, adjust scoring weights.
5) Gradual rollout by region and instance family.

Rollback conditions: sustained increase in p95 >10% for 30 minutes, error-rate spike, or probe overhead exceeding 1% of capacity.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: probes contribute to tail; Mitigation: run probes in background priority class and limit per-node concurrency.
- Risk: noisy early estimates cause instability; Mitigation: require minimum sample count and apply damping to weight updates.
- Risk: cross-tenant interference on shared pools; Mitigation: per-customer isolation flags and disable sculptor for dedicated clusters unless explicitly allowed.
